newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil secures first syndicated loan since 1982.
newsitem.headline: Brazil secures first syndicated loan since 1982.

text.p: A group of 26 foreign banks led by Bankers Trust New York Corp granted Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) the country's first sovereign syndicated loan in 15 years, a development bank official said on Thursday.

BNDES Finance Director Jose Mauro Carneiro da Cunha said it was the first medium-term loan granted by international banks to the development bank since Brazil declared a moratorium on foreign debt payments in 1982.
"We consider this a very important event because it is the first time in 15 years that we have carried out an operation of this nature," Carneiro said in a news conference.
Carneiro said the deal was an eight-year loan, redeemable after three years and would pay interest of 1.625 percentage points over the benchmark Libor rate.
Originally set at two percentage points over Libor, Carneiro said the interest rate was lowered after Standard & Poor's raised Brazil's corporate debt rating to BB-minus from B-plus last week.
Carneiro said the development bank would use the $275 million to help finance its $3 billion 1997 loan portfolio and fund long-term projects in industry and infrastructure.
He said several of the financial institutions participating in the deal were lending to Brazil for the first time.
Brazil returned to international capital markets in 1991 and a year later rescheduled $49 billion of its foreign debt under a Brady-style deal.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 507 4151))
